prompt: A mobile landing page at phone viewport, portrait, for Wander Niagara, rendered edge to edge as a real web page with crisp readable text, no phone frame, no browser chrome. The page is a house seen from the bottom of its own front steps: the visitor is planning a winter day trip or overnight to St. Catharines and the Benchlands and chooses a room to enter. Parts in reading order: a slim header on the night sky with a small white "Wander" wordmark at left and one small engraved brass plaque button "What's on" at right. Below it, from a low angle on the front walk looking up, a red-brick Georgian colonial at night: the black six-panel front door with a full evergreen wreath and red velvet bow and a lit brass lantern dominates the upper half of the screen under its white arched portico; the dining-room window at left with a crystal chandelier and the living-room window at right with a lit tree glow amber through sheer curtains at the edges; two dormers glow above at the very top. Warm-white mini-lights outline the windows and arch; snow on every ledge; slow falling snow. The brick steps come down toward the viewer with black iron railings, and on the left railing five engraved brass plaques are mounted one above another, reading "What's on this winter", "Eat, drink and shop", "Winter outdoors", "Stay the night", "Winter reading". At the bottom, in the deep blue-shadowed snow of the walk, as set type: the headline "Winter is made for wandering" and the subline "A holiday escape to St. Catharines and the Benchlands." Visual law: a warm navy night sky, never black. A heavy, friendly 1990 greeting-card serif in snow white. Brass plaques with engraved lettering. Warm inside, cold outside; film-grain warmth.
